text: Plant cells contain an enzyme, catalase, which catalyses the breakdown of hydrogen
peroxide into oxygen and water.
You are required
• to immobilise the catalase in sodium alginate beads
• to investigate the independent variable, hydrogen peroxide concentration.
When a bead is dropped into hydrogen peroxide it will sink and then the release of oxygen
causes the bead to rise.
You are provided with
• 50 cm of 10 % hydrogen peroxide solution, labelled H
• 100 cm of distilled water, labelled W
• 10 cm of a plant extract containing catalase, labelled P
• 15 cm of 2 % sodium alginate solution, labelled S
• 30 cm of 1.5 % calcium chloride solution, labelled C.
Proceed as follows:
1. Put 10 cm of C into a large test-tube.
2. Put 5 cm of S into a small beaker.
3. Put 3 cm of P into the same beaker and mix well.
4. Use a 5 cm syringe to collect 2 cm of the mixture, S and P.
5. Suspend the 5 cm syringe over the large test-tube containing C as shown in Fig. 1.1.
